Replanned Wed Nov 11 · Tue Nov 10 – Fri Nov 13, 2026 · 3 people

Vancouver in four rainy, brilliant days

Rebuilt again on Wednesday, to your list: the Vancouver Lookout is out, Lynn Canyon's suspension bridge is back in, and FlyOver Canada joins today. Today (Wed, rain) is FlyOver, Stanley Park and as many beaches as the weather allows in rain gear, the Lynn Canyon bridge, and Gastown. Thursday — the one dry day — is the big one: Skylynx to Squamish, Shannon Falls and the Sea to Sky Gondola in the morning, then Kitsilano, Jericho and the English Bay sunset done properly, finishing with the birthday dinner in Gastown (the ramen dinner is gone — the birthday replaces it). No car, beginner-friendly, student budget, based at the Atrium Hotel.

Base · Atrium Hotel, 2889 E Hastings St Today Wed · Rain 100% — FlyOver, Stanley Park, beaches push, Lynn Canyon, Gastown Thu Nov 12 · Dry day — gondola + Squamish + all 3 beaches + birthday in Gastown Leave · Fri 9:00 AM for the airport Sunset · ~5:35 PM Wed · 5:33 PM Thu

Why Days 2 and 3 were rebuilt — again, to your list

Tuesday's rain rewrote the trip: Gastown never happened, Kitsilano was a restaurant stop instead of the beach, and Jericho was skipped outright. Your calls for this version: no Vancouver Lookout, Lynn Canyon stays, no ramen — the birthday dinner moves to Day 3 in Gastown — and Thursday carries everything at once: Skylynx, Squamish, the gondola and all three beaches, because Thursday is the only dry day to put them on.

Today: rain, 100%

Wednesday is rain all day (100%, heavier again tonight). Today mixes covered stops with a deliberate rain-gear push: FlyOver Canada is fully indoors, Stanley Park's seawall is paved and half-sheltered by the canopy, English Bay (and Kits, if the rain eases) are walks not sits, and Lynn Canyon is kept to the bridge itself plus the Ecology Centre. If the rain peaks at midday, the Bloedel dome is the built-in swap.

Thursday: everything, on the dry day

Thu Nov 12 is cloudy with only a 20% chance of rain — the only dry window of the trip, so it gets the best-weather stack: the gondola and Squamish in the morning light, then Kits, Jericho and English Bay in the afternoon, sunset at 5:33 PM, birthday dinner after.

Birthday: Gastown, on Day 3

Moved from tonight to Thursday night, as asked — and it lands better there: you come off the English Bay sunset straight into Gastown, the Steam Clock lit and steaming, for the birthday dinner. The ramen dinner that was Thursday's plan is removed to make room.

Wed is Remembrance Day

Nov 11 is a BC stat holiday: transit runs a Sunday schedule (leave buffer time), attractions stay open, and there's a public ceremony at Victory Square at 10 AM — right on your bus route downtown.

Day 1 · Tue Nov 10Heavy rain — market & covered stops leadDay total ~$67 / person — see breakdown below

Market morning, two beaches, downtown after dark — hour by hour

The wettest day starts under a roof: Granville Island Public Market — the fishermen's market from your list, with working fish stalls on the dockside. Then the west-side beaches while you're already over there, and Gastown to finish. Every leg below shows travel time + travel cost; every stop shows entry / activity cost. All city transit today is covered by one DayPass — you don't pay per ride after 10:30 AM.

What actually happened (Tue Nov 10): the rain won the second half of this day. Granville Island and the market happened, and you ate in Kitsilano — but Kits Beach itself was never walked, Jericho Beach was skipped entirely, and Gastown never happened. The timeline below is the original plan, kept as the record; the misses are recovered in the new plan — Gastown is recovered on Day 2 (Wed) and again for the Day 3 birthday dinner, and Kits Beach properly + Jericho move to Day 3 (Thu), the dry day, alongside the gondola. (The Vancouver Lookout, which sat in earlier versions of this plan, is now removed entirely, at your request.)

Day 2 · Wed Nov 11Remembrance Day · rain 100% — indoor first, park & beaches in rain gearDay total ~$83 / person · +$9 if you take the dome swap

FlyOver, Stanley Park & the beaches push, Lynn Canyon bridge, Gastown

Today replaces the old North Shore plan on your instructions: the Lookout is gone, Lynn Canyon's suspension bridge is in, FlyOver Canada joins the morning, and — your latest call — Stanley Park and as many beaches as the weather allows are attempted today, not saved for Thursday. The shape: ceremony glimpse and FlyOver first (both downtown, one covered), then Stanley Park and English Bay in rain gear — the park canopy and the paved seawall are the most doable outdoor stops in the city in rain — a weather-dependent push over the bridge to Kits, then the Lynn Canyon bridge in the late afternoon, and Gastown to finish. Tomorrow still repeats the beaches properly, dry.

The honest weather note: today is 100% rain, so the park-and-beaches block is a rain-gear push, not a picnic — waterproof shoes, jackets on, and the stops are walks, not sits. It works because Stanley Park's seawall is paved and half-sheltered by the tree canopy, and English Bay is 10 minutes from the park's south end. If the rain peaks hard around midday, the built-in swap is the Bloedel Conservatory (the heated tropical dome at Queen Elizabeth Park, ~$9, 45 min by transit) in place of the Kits push — the park and English Bay still stand, and Kits gets its full dry version tomorrow either way.

Day 3 · Thu Nov 12The dry day — cloudy, rain only 20% · best weather of the tripDay total ~$183 / person

The big day: Skylynx, Squamish & the gondola — then all three beaches — then the birthday in Gastown

Everything you listed, on the one day the weather allows it. Morning: the Skylynx coach up the Sea-to-Sky highway to Squamish, Shannon Falls thundering after the week's rain, and the Sea to Sky Gondola summit while the light is best. Afternoon: back downtown and straight into the beach chain — Kitsilano walked properly, Jericho recovered in full, and the English Bay sunset at 5:33 PM. Evening: the birthday dinner in Gastown, which replaces the ramen dinner outright — ramen is off the plan. It is a packed day by design; the flex rules are in the alert below.

How this day holds together: the hinge is the Skylynx return. The timeline assumes an early-afternoon return (~1:00 PM) — confirm the Winter 2026/27 timetable on yvrskylynx.com tonight and book the earliest return that still gives you the summit. If the only return is ~2:00 PM, everything after shifts an hour: Kits and English Bay still happen, Jericho shortens to ~30 minutes. What never gets cut: the gondola morning and the Gastown birthday dinner. Stanley Park had its full visit yesterday, so today the park is the seawall pass into English Bay, not a second long stop.

If Thursday's forecast falls apart overnight

Check before the 7 AM bus. If the 20% has blown up into real rain: the gondola still runs (the summit in cloud is moody, not cancelled), but the beaches shrink to English Bay only and Jericho / the Kits redo drop — they were already covered on Day 2's push and Day 1. The birthday dinner doesn't move. Decide at breakfast, with the actual sky in front of you, and rebook the Skylynx return earlier if you shorten the day.

Why not Whistler instead?

The same Skylynx continues to Whistler for the same $42 round trip — but mid-November is Whistler's quiet gap: the ski season typically opens in late November, the village is a long way to go for a stroll, and a Whistler day would eat the beaches and the birthday timing. Squamish is half the travel, has the gondola and the falls, and gets you back for sunset.

Above: the Sea to Sky Gondola above Howe Sound (left) and Jericho Beach (right), where the downtown skyline lines up across the bay — Thursday's two ends of the day, summit in the morning, sand in the afternoon.

Your TikTok list, judged honestly

Everything you saved, sorted for this trip: 2½ real days, November weather, no car, beginner hikers. Nothing here is a bad place — some of it is just a different season or a different trip.

In the plan

  • Granville Island Public Market — your "fishermen's market"Day 1 — the real thing: fish stalls on the dockside, lunch in the covered hall. The one stop Tuesday's rain couldn't touch.
  • FlyOver Canada — Canada PlaceDay 2 — the indoor flying-theatre ride, added at your request: the perfect 100%-rain headliner. From $31 online vs $38 at the gate; the Rockies film is showing in this window.
  • Lynn Canyon Suspension BridgeDay 2 — kept, as you insisted: free, 50 m over the gorge, dramatic after rain. Kept to the bridge + boardwalk loop, with the lower gorge trails off-limits in the wet.
  • Stanley Park — Totem Poles, Brockton Point & Prospect PointDay 2 — a full east-side visit in daylight (your latest call: the park today, not just Thursday), plus the Day 3 seawall pass into English Bay.
  • Kitsilano Beach ParkDay 2 weather permitting, and Day 3 properly: the full shoreline walk on the dry day, first beach of the afternoon chain.
  • Jericho Beach ParkDay 3 — the stop skipped entirely on Day 1, recovered in full: the skyline-from-the-sand view in the late light.
  • English Bay BeachDay 2 in rain gear, and Day 3 as the sunset finale at 5:33 PM — the trip's closing daylight.
  • Sea to Sky Gondola + Shannon Falls + Skylynx to SquamishDay 3, in the plan (no longer a swap): the dry morning is the best weather of the trip, and the summit, the falls and the coach are all on it. $73.95 online + $42 coach.
  • Gastown + Steam ClockDay 2 evening wander, recovered — and Day 3 night: the birthday dinner on Water Street, replacing the ramen dinner.

Only if…

  • Bloedel Conservatory — your "Dome Vancouver"Day 2's built-in rain swap: if Wednesday's rain peaks at midday, the heated tropical dome (~$9) replaces the Kits push. Otherwise Thursday's dry beach version wins.
  • Horseshoe Bay + Porteau CoveThrough the Skylynx window on Day 3 — the Sea-to-Sky highway passes both; left-side seats.
  • Grouse MountainOnly if the webcam shows clear sky — $89 is too much for fog, and both remaining days are full. The Gravity Coaster and ziplines are warm-season; skiing usually starts later in November.
  • Capilano Suspension BridgeGenuinely fun, but $76.95 + GST ≈ $80.80 ($65.95 student + GST) — and Lynn Canyon gives you a suspension bridge over a gorge for $0 on Day 2. Go only if Capilano itself is the bucket-list item.
  • WhistlerSame coach, same $42 — but it's the off-season gap before skiing starts, and it would eat Day 3's beaches and birthday timing. Squamish wins this trip.
  • Bowen IslandDoable car-free (257 bus + ferry, $12.45 return, 20-min crossing) as a swap day — but it's a summer island; in November rain it's a quiet village and a nice ferry ride.
  • Squamish Canyon / Mamquam FallsBoth need a car or taxi hop once you're in Squamish, and Day 3's coach timing leaves no room. First add-ons if you ever repeat the corridor with a car.
  • Deep Cove + Quarry RockWas Day 2 in the oldest plan — out: forest stairs and roots in 100% rain, and both replanned days are full without it. First stop on a drier return trip; free.

Not this trip

  • Vancouver LookoutRemoved at your request in this version — it sat in earlier plans at $16.93 student / $23.88 adult; your call was to spend that slot on FlyOver and Lynn Canyon instead.
  • Tulip festivalIt's April. There are no tulips in November — TikTok lied by omission.
  • Joffre LakesNeeds a pre-booked BC Parks day pass, ~2½–3 hrs each way past Squamish with no transit option, and icy alpine trails in November.
  • Wedgemount LakeOne of the hardest hikes in the corridor — 7+ hrs and 1,100 m of climbing, in snow. Not a beginner trail in any season.
  • Lindeman LakeOut by Chilliwack — car-only, wrong direction, half the day gone in travel.
  • Victoria3½–4 hrs each way by bus and ferry — that's your entire trip spent travelling. Save it for a 2-day trip of its own.
  • Kelowna4½–5 hrs each way through mountain passes. A separate trip, full stop.
  • The trestle bridge (Kinsol Trestle)It's on Vancouver Island — ferry + car territory.
  • Pitt Lake · Bridal Falls · Tsawwassen BeachCar-only or bus marathons at the far edges of the region, with nothing November-specific to earn the hours.
  • Lighthouse Park · Cypress Falls · Whytecliff · Larsons ParkAll West Vancouver — each is a half-day by bus, and the replanned days have no room: Wednesday is FlyOver / park / Lynn Canyon / Gastown and Thursday is the gondola-beaches-birthday stack. These are for a trip with a car.

Fare smarts: a Compass DayPass is $12.55 for unlimited all-zone travel and pays for itself by your third ride of the day — buy one Tue, Wed and Thu. Leaving YVR on Day 1 costs $19.05 in total: the $6.50 YVR AddFare is charged on top of the DayPass when you buy it at YVR / Sea Island stations — a DayPass bought there does not dodge it. Single rides on a Compass Card are $2.85 (1 zone); buses are always charged as 1 zone, and after 6:30 PM the whole system drops to 1-zone fares. You can also just tap a bank card, but you'll pay the higher cash fare each time.

Book or check before you go

  • Book the Skylynx round trip — tonight (Wed), on yvrskylynx.com. 8:00 AM out Thu, and the earliest afternoon return that still gives you the summit (~1:00 PM in the plan). Confirm the Winter 2026/27 timetable before paying — Day 3's beach timing hangs on that return.
  • Book Sea to Sky Gondola tickets online — tonight. $73.95 online vs $81.95 at the window; open 9 AM–5 PM, last ride down 6 PM, open through Nov 15.
  • Book the Gastown birthday table — for Thu ~6:45 PM, 3 people. Mention the birthday when you book. This replaces the ramen plan — no Denman Street queue on the birthday night.
  • Book FlyOver Canada online for Wed ~10 AM. From $31 online vs $38 at the gate; check which film is showing (the Rockies film runs Nov 2–18).
  • Check Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre hours before Wednesday's afternoon leg — the bridge is the point either way; the centre is the bonus. And check Thursday's forecast again at Wednesday bedtime: the 20% holding is what makes Day 3 the best-weather stack.
  • Return flight time, Thursday night — confirm it before you set Friday's alarm.

Pack for a wet November week

  • Waterproof shoes or boots — Wednesday's Gastown cobblestones are slick when wet, Lynn Canyon's boardwalk is wet wood, and the beaches are wet sand and logs; this is the single most important item.
  • A real rain jacket + an umbrella each — Wednesday is rain all day and the park-and-beaches push happens in it: the jacket is for the seawall, the umbrella is for the ceremony and the Gastown door-to-door hops.
  • One warm layer, plus hat/gloves if you have them — Thursday's gondola summit sits near 0° with wind; the beaches catch the breeze off the bay.
  • Student ID — no student fare at FlyOver or the gondola, but it still earns discounts around the city (and Capilano's student fare if that ever replaces Lynn Canyon).
  • A small daypack each — for layers, water, and Thursday's summit-to-beach gear changes.
